title: Advanced Tier Architecture and Bundle Optimization
description: Master complex packaging decisions involving tier economics, feature gating tradeoffs, and enterprise vs self-serve channel design.

interactions.prompt: A B2B analytics platform has three tiers: Starter ($49/mo, 68% of users), Pro ($149/mo, 24% of users), Growth ($399/mo, 8% of users). Starter-to-Pro conversion is 11%, but Pro-to-Growth is only 1.8%. What's the critical signal?

options.text: Starter price is too low, causing anchor bias
The Pro-to-Growth gap reveals a missing tier or broken upsell path
Growth tier needs more features to justify the price
68% Starter concentration means freemium would work better

interactions.prompt: Your SaaS product gates SSO behind the Enterprise tier ($800/mo). A competitor just ungated SSO across all tiers. Your mid-market pipeline has slowed 30%. You have limited engineering bandwidth for new features.

options.text: Ungate SSO but introduce a new security bundle as an add-on
Keep SSO gated but drop Enterprise price to $550/mo
Move SSO to Pro tier, gate advanced SCIM/audit logs at Enterprise
Ungate SSO entirely and raise base prices across all tiers by 15%

interactions.prompt: When designing a Good-Better-Best tier structure, the middle tier should capture the majority of revenue through ____, where the top tier's high price makes the middle tier feel like a rational compromise.

options.text: Decoy pricing
The asymmetric dominance effect
The compromise effect
Value metric anchoring

interactions.prompt: A PLG company averaging $12K ACV wants to build an enterprise motion ($80K+ ACV). Rank these packaging changes by impact on enterprise deal acceleration: (a) Add volume discount tiers, (b) Create custom bundle builder for procurement, (c) Introduce usage-committed annual contracts with overage billing, (d) Gate admin/governance features behind enterprise tier.

options.text: Add volume discount tiers
Create custom bundle builder for procurement
Introduce usage-committed annual contracts with overage billing
Gate admin/governance features behind enterprise tier

interactions.prompt: Datadog's 2023 10-K shows customers using 2+ products grew from 75% to 82% YoY, while customers using 4+ products grew from 33% to 44%. Average ARR per customer rose 20% despite flat seat growth. What packaging insight does this reveal?

options.text: Price increases are the primary ARR expansion driver
Cross-product bundling and integrated workflows drive net dollar expansion without seat growth
Customers are consolidating vendors, reducing Datadog's competitive moat
Flat seat growth signals an upcoming churn risk at renewal

interactions.prompt: You're CPO at a $50M ARR collaboration tool. Self-serve generates 70% of new logos but only 35% of revenue. Enterprise sales drives 65% of revenue but CAC payback is 18 months vs 4 months for self-serve. Board wants faster growth and better unit economics simultaneously.

options.text: Cap self-serve at 50 seats, forcing larger teams into sales-assisted
Build an automated expansion path with in-product upgrade triggers at usage thresholds
Shift enterprise reps to manage only $100K+ pipeline, automate the rest
Bundle enterprise features into self-serve at higher prices to reduce sales dependency

interactions.prompt: You're restructuring bundles for a $30M ARR DevOps platform. Rank these metrics by importance for validating whether your new packaging is working: (a) Logo acquisition rate, (b) Expansion revenue as % of total new ARR, (c) Time from first tier to second tier upgrade, (d) Gross margin per tier.

options.text: Logo acquisition rate
Expansion revenue as % of total new ARR
Time from first tier to second tier upgrade
Gross margin per tier

interactions.prompt: Your largest competitor just launched a flat-rate unlimited plan at $299/user/mo, collapsing their three tiers. Social media is buzzing. Your usage-based Pro tier customers (40% of ARR) are asking if you'll match. What's your counter-move?

options.text: Launch a comparable flat-rate plan but limit it to annual commitments only
Introduce a predictable-spend cap on your usage tier so customers get upside protection
Ignore it—flat-rate commoditizes value and the competitor will face margin pressure
Bundle two products into your Pro tier at current price to increase switching costs

interactions.priorContext: You previously optimized your packaging around usage-based pricing with strong expansion economics. Now a competitor has disrupted market expectations with flat-rate simplicity, threatening your core pricing model and creating customer uncertainty.
